established_from_source: run_shared_identity_experiment.py:39-47 invokes the R201E loss closure inside torch.autocast(cuda). smooth_ap disables autocast and casts to float for its entire forward at list_retrieval_objective.py:14-30. Returning to run_r201e_list_objective.py:46 restores the outer enabled context for this unscaled autograd.grad diagnostic.

The actual full-loss scaled backward is outside that context at run_shared_identity_experiment.py:48-50; the partial backward and single optimizer step remain at lines54-64. The diagnostic therefore uses a different autocast context from the eventual training backward. This difference is real; it is not evidence that a particular backward kernel actually underflowed.

The differentiated feature is the first returned fused descriptor at rgbnt201_identity_outlet.py:89,106. Its fuse computes in disabled autocast, converts operands to float and returns F.normalize(private) at lines31-53. Thus the current feature and the SmoothAP forward are FP32 by source. An enabled surrounding context alone does not establish that the returned gradient, or every backward operation, was FP16.

The SmoothAP graph remains connected through normalization, cosine products, score differences, sigmoid and ratios. The existing CPU check exercises one random value/gradient case and separated/tied loss values; it does not establish a nonzero derivative on the real pretrained native batch.

Only the primary full-view metric term changes relative to R201C narrow/unit; .25 CE, AP coefficient1, temperature.01, auxiliary losses, partial losses, targets, routes, frozen anchor and model/budget remain unchanged in the five verified sources.
source_supported_hypotheses_not_runtime_: The diagnostic autocast context can be tested as a precision confound. FP32 forward computation does not justify assuming that running autograd.grad under enabled autocast is equivalent to the real outside-autocast backward. Whether this produces underflow or another numerical change in this environment is UNKNOWN until the paired probe is run.

A small-temperature ranking objective on this actual feature geometry can have a numerically zero or very small derivative. The existing fixture reports perfect_loss=0 for separated features, but the failed native logs report neither AP loss nor margins nor any gradient statistics. Actual saturation, cancellation, nonfinite values, and their relative contribution remain UNKNOWN.

probe_list_gradient_precision.py:33-39 executes one model full-view forward and one smooth_ap call. It requests both derivatives of the same scalar loss with respect to the same output[1] tensor, uses retain_graph=True, and changes only the autocast context between requests. No detach/recreated leaf/recomputed forward changes the tested graph.

The disabled context does not rerun the backbone in FP32. It compares backward contexts on the existing mixed-precision model forward followed by the FP32 AP computation. This is exactly the relevant diagnostic distinction.

No optimizer is constructed or stepped; there is no model checkpoint write, parameter-gradient accumulation via backward, partial forward, training loop or native/formal acceptance claim. The train-mode forward can update in-memory BatchNorm buffers; those are not persisted.

probe_list_gradient_precision.py:47-56 records finite/l1/maximum/dtype/nonzero for both gradients, maximum difference, primary AP loss, actual unit-descriptor feature_dtype, identity counts, all per-query positive counts, names, and min/mean/max margins.

Lines40-46 recompute normalized FP32 cosine scores for reporting only. Positives include same-ID other samples and exclude the diagonal; negatives exclude the same identity. The margin is min positive similarity minus max negative similarity per query. It is a separation diagnostic, not proof of sigmoid saturation.

A loss rounded to zero is not itself proof of zero derivative. If both recorded derivatives are zero, the probe establishes numerical zero at this feature in the deployed FP32 implementation, not an identically zero mathematical objective. If both are nonzero, the first-batch assertion failure was not reproduced.
